arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: The father's advocate stated the mother kidnapped the daughter. He said she concealed her in the UK, France, and the US.
The mother's advocate argued equitable tolling contradicts the treaty. She cited the Convention's text and drafting history.
Justice Ginsburg asked where Article 13 appears in the materials. She emphasized the paramount importance of the child's interest.
Justice Scalia asked where the relevant text is located. He sought specific reference points in the case record.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case tests whether equitable tolling applies to the Hague Convention. This doctrine pauses deadlines when a party hides evidence. The father argues concealment justifies a return. The mother argues the treaty text forbids this delay.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: The father wants the court to apply equitable tolling. He seeks the return of his daughter to his custody.
The mother wants the court to reject equitable tolling. She seeks to keep her daughter in the United States.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: The father argues concealment stopped the one-year deadline. He claims the mother hid the child for years.
The mother argues the treaty text forbids extending deadlines. She claims other signatory states reject this interpretation.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Justice Alito asked if the opposing side's position incentivizes child abduction. He noted parents might hide children to delay proceedings.
Justice Kennedy asked if the court uses equitable discretion or tolling. He questioned how a six-month suspension affects the weighing process.
